senses.gloss: abandoning, giving up, renouncing (in favor of the poor, Lev. XIX, 10).
units: <cite ref="Chullin 131b:3">Ḥull. 131ᵇ</cite> <he>וכולן … מ״ט ע׳ כתיב בהו</he> and from all of them the owner must not derive the benefit of putting a person under obligation (v. <cite ref="I00112"><he>טוֹבָה</he></cite>), because ‘abandoning’ (<he>עזב</he>) is written about them (Lev. l. c.). Y. Peah IV, end, 19ᵃ <he>שהן בע׳</he> they must be abandoned. Ib. V, beg. 19ᵇ (ref. to <he>תעזב אתם</he>, Lev. l. c.) <he>יש לך ע׳ אחרת כזו</he> (it intimates that) there is another abandonment like this (renouncing one’s property in favor of the poor, v. <cite ref="E00759"><he>הֶפְקֵר</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 11:3:2">Y. Ned. XI, 42ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>מעשר עני ניתן בזכייה ואלו בע׳</he> the tithe of the poor is given to the poor by way of a transfer (to a certain person), but these (gifts) are abandoned (the owner having no right of disposal).
<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 5:20">Lam. R. to V, 20</cite> <he>ארבעה דברים</he> … <he>מאיסה וגעילה ע׳ ושכיחה</he> Jeremiah used four expressions: rejection, loathing, forsaking, and forgetting.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 69:6">Gen. R. s. 69</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 28:15">Gen. XXVIII, 15</cite>) <he>אין ע׳ אלא פרנסה</he> forsaking refers to sustenance (with ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 37:25">Ps. XXXVII, 25</cite>); <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 35:2">Lev. R. s. 35</cite>; a. e.
<cite ref="Nedarim 22a:1">Ned. 22ᵃ</cite> (in Chald. dict.) <he>מלין דע׳</he> things which must be shunned (indecencies); (Ar. <he>מלין דעֲזוּבָה</he> things worthy of an abandoned woman).
